The capital city of France is Paris.
Paris, officially known as "La République française," was founded in 843 AD when Charlemagne ruled over real estate in the area that would later become today's French and German-speaking regions (Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland). It quickly became one of Europe’s most important cities due to its strategic location along the Atlantic coast from Northern Italy through Germany to Eastern Europe.

Since then, it has grown tremendously, becoming more and more famous for its architecture, art, music, literature, theater, fashion, food culture, cinema, gastronomy, sport, sports events, science, technology, film industry, history, etc., with many outstanding UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Today, Paris thrives on a unique historical context combined with modern innovation; therefore, it outshines any other major European urban centers like London or Rome. The city stands proud against all challenges; these include strongly favorable climate conditions conducive to living, advanced infrastructure, excellent public services, wide variety of recreational activities, cultural amenities, splendid natural environment, strong sense of identity, rich tradition, understanding between regional cultures, international cooperation among nations, political stability, longevity under various climates, continuous evolution without facing obstacles such as war, economic crisis, environmental pollution or disasters. In short, there is no better place than Paris to enjoy life!
